, PART II — Advertisements, Notices 

Procedure regarding sending Manuscripts for publication of Advertisements, Notices, etc., in 

the “Calcutta Gazette” (Part II). 

1. Manuscripts should be propsrly edited and oomplete In itself. 

• • 

‘2. Manuscripts should always be typewritten on one side of the paper. Che name of the signatory should be type 
written* below the signature. 

3. Manusorlpts Intended for advertisement in the next issue of “Calcutta Gazette" shall be received by Publication 
ss'Qfnoe at Writers' Buildings up to 12 noon on Saturday and at Head Office at Alipore up to 12 noon on Monday. 

4. All costs shall be paid In advance and deposited along with the Manuscripts. 

5. Manusorlpts and postal remittances shall be addressed to SUPERINTENDENT, GOVERNMENT printing 
JBLICATION BRANCH), WE8T BENGAL GOVERNMENT PRESS, ALIPORE. 

The Press shall not be held responsible for delay In publication of any advertisement due to the non-observanoo of the 
(motions detailed above.

NOTIFICATION No. 1313— HD/5P-8/53. 

Calcutta, the 1st July 1953. 

1. Applications are invited for admission to the Prinoe of Wales’s Military College. 
Dehra Dun, for the oouree commencing in January 1954. 

2. The College, which is under the direct control of tho General Headquarters 
provides a public school education for boys who wish to obtain commissions in the 
Array, Navy or Air Force. The educational training is designed to bring boys up to 
the standard of the Senior Cambridge School Certificate and the Qualifying Examina- 
tions for ontry into tho National Defence Academy. Compulsory physical training, 
games and parades are arranged to ensure physical fitness and smartness; while special 
attention is paid to the imparting of discipline, self-reliance and social training to all 
eadote. 


3. Admission to the Prinoe of Wales’s Military College will be made through an 
examination followed by an interview by a Selection Board, at Caloutta. in the 
3rd week of September 1953. 

4. Candidates for admission to this examination must have been born not earlier 
than the 21st January 1942 and not later than tho 20th January 1943 The age limits 
oan in no case be relaxed. 

5. A candidate must be an unmarried male and must either bo — 

(a) a citizen of India, or 

(h) a person who has migrated from Pakistan with the intention of permanently

APPENDIX 1. 


Physical condition for admission to the Prinoe of Wales's Military College, Dehra Dun. 

1. To he passed as fit for admission to the Prince oi Wales’s Military College, a 
candidate must he in good mental and bodily health, and free from any physical delect 
likely to interfere with the efficient performance of glilitary duty. 

9 2. A standard for height and chest measurement and physical development cannot 

he laid down, but the candidate should not be below the nverag© for his age and rare. 

«*i. The candidate’s height will he measured as follows: — 

Hj; will he , placed against the standard with his feet together, and the weight, 
thrown on the heeds and not on tlfe toes or outer sides of the loot. He will stand 
erect, without rigidity ^ind with the heels, calves, buttocks and shoulders touching the 
standard; the cliin will he depressed to bring the vertex of the head level under the 
horizontal bar, and the height will Ik? recorded in inches and parts of an meh to 
quarters. 

4. The candidate’s chest will 1 a? measured as follows: — 

He will he made to stand erect with his feet together, and to raise his arms over 
his head. The tape will be so adjusted round the chest that its upper edge touches, 
the inferior angles of the shoulder-blades behind, and its "lower edge the upper part 
of the nipples in front. The arms will then he lowered to hang loosely by the side, 
and care \vill he taken that the shoulders are uot thrown upwards or backwards ho as to 
displace' the tape. The candidate will then he directed to take a deep inspiration 
several times, and the maximum expansion of the chest will he careiully noted The 
minimum and maximum will then be recorded. In recording the measurements, 
fractions of less than half an inch should not he rioted. 

5. The candidate, will also be weighed, and Ins weight recorded in pounds. Frac- 
tions of a pound should not bo noted. 

6. The examination for determining the acuteneHs of vision includes two tests, one 
for distant, the otiier for near vision. The Snellen’s type should ho used for the tost, 
for distiyit vision, without glasses at a distance of 20 feet, and for the test tor near 
vision without glasses, at any distance selected by the candidate. The standards of 
the minimum acuteness of vision with which a candidate will he considered fit are. — 


Better eyo. Worse eye. 

Distant vision — V-6/6. Distant vision not below 0/60. 

After correction with glasses not below 0/18. 
Near vision reads 0 6. * Near ’vision reads 0’6 


Each eye must have a full field of vision as tested by hand movements. 

Squint or any morbid condition of the eyes or of the lid of either eye liable to the 
risk of aggravation or recurrence will cause rejection of the candidate. 

Each eye will be examined separately. The candidate will he required to road the 
tests in ordinary daylight. • 

Inability to distinguish ^the principal colours will not he regarded as cause for 
rejection but the fact will be noted ip the proceedings and the candidate informed. 

N6 relaxation of the standard of vision will be allowed.

(a) .That his. hearing is good. (The ears should bo examined internally with an 

auroscope.) 

(b) That his speech is without impediment. 

(c) -That his teeth are in good order. Ho must have 10 sound teeth in the uj»per 

jaw functionally opposed to 10 sound teeth in the lower jaw. Two of these 
teeth in each jaw must be molars. Well filled teeth will he considered as 
sound. 

(d) That his chest is well formed and that his lungs and heart are sound. 

(e) That ho is not ruptured. 

(/) That ho does not suffer from a severe degree of varicocele* or varicose veins.

(3) Instructions regarding submission of applications. 

Applications are to be made ou the prescribed form (West 
Bengal Form No. 969) which has been made saleable and 
priced annas two per copy to make it readily availuble to 
candidates. It will be available on payment from the 
following places: — Office of the Public Service Commission, 
West Bengal, Anderson House (ground floor), Alipure, 
Calcutta-27, all District Treasuries and Hub-Treasuries in 
West Bengal, the Sales Depot of the Publication Branch. 
Writers’ Buildings, Calcutta. Persons registered at the 
Employment Exchange, Calcutta, may obtain the form 
from that office. Persons residing outside West Bengal 
may obtain the form from the office of the Commi^ion on 
■ending the price of the form in stamps ol denomination 
of six pies only. A large self-addressed envelope with 
■tamps, sufficient to cover the postage affixed to it, must 
accompany every request for the supply of the form. 
Candidates who are unable to obtain copies of the pres- 
cribed form may apply on any similar typed (not hand- 
Written) form, showing exactly the wording and spacing 
of the sample form published in the “Calcutta Gazette'’ 
of the 10th March 1949, provided the blanks are filled up 
in the candidates’ own handwriting. 

The applications must lie addressed to the Secretary and 
should reach lum not later than the ]0th August 1953. 

(4) Particulars and oertffloates required.— Candidates 
Bhould furnish evidence of their age, qualifications and 
previous experience together with certificates written not 
more than one year prior to the date of their applications, 
from responsible persons, testifying to their private 
character. 

• 

(6) FM. — Candidates must enclose with their applies 
tions a fee of Bs. 5 in the form of * receipted 
chalan from a Government Treasury or the Reserve 
Bank of India under the head “XXXVI — Miscel- 
laneous — Receipts of the Public Service Commission, West 
Bengal”. Money orders, cheques, etc., in lieu ot Treasury 
chalans are not acceptor!. Postal orders, however, may he 
accepted from candidates. They should be crossed and 
made payable to “the Hocretary, Public Service Commission. 
West Bengal”. No application will be considered unless 
accompanied with the requisite application fee. 

Candidates in Government service should make sure 
before depositing fee that their applications will be 
forwarded by their superior officers. In nb case will the 
fee paid with the application be refunded. 

(6) Address. — Candidates should give their present 
add ress and should communicate at once any subsequent 
change of uddrcsH. 

(7) Canvassing. — Any uttempt ou the part ol candidate- 
to enlist support ot their applications through persons ot 
influence or olfuials oi Government will disquality tiiem 
for appointment. ^Spontaneous recommendation irom 
persons interested in the candidates or otherwise known to 
them will be disregarded. 

(8) Applications from candidates who are in permanent 
or temporary employment under any Government, a local 
or Statutory Body (e.g., Damodar Valley Corporation), in 
India will bo rejected unless they arc submitted through 
the appointing authority of their posts or service.

Calcutta , the 1st July 1953. 

1. Applications are invited for admission to the Prinoe of Wales’s Military College, 
Dehra Dun, for the oouree oommenoing in January 1954. 

2. The College, which is under the direct control of the General Headquarters 
provides a public school education for boys who wish to obtain commissions in the 
Army, Navy or Air Force. The educational training is designed to bring boys up to 
tho standard of the Senior Cambridge School Certificate and the Qualifying Examina- 
tions for entry into the National Defence Academy. Compulsory physical training, 
games and parades are arranged to ensure physical fitness and smartness ; while special 
attention is paid to the imparting of discipline, self-reliance and Boeial training to all 
cadets. 


8. Admission to the Prinoe of Wales's Military College will b9 made through an 
examination followed by an interview by a Selection Board, at Calcutta, in the 
3rd week of September 1953. 

4. Candidates for admission to this examination must have been born not earlier 
than tbo 21st January 1942 and not later than the 20th January 1943. The age Imilte 

oan in no case be relaxed. 


5. A candidate must bo an unmarried male and must either be — 

(a) a citizen of India, or 

(b) a person who haH migrated from Pakistan with the intention of permanently 

settling in India, 

and he must be domiciled in Vfcst Bengal. If he comes under category (6) must be a 
person in whose lavour a certificate of eligibility has been given by the Government 
oi India. A candidate in whose case such a certificate is necessary may be provisionally 
admitted to the College subject to the necessary certificate being eventually given to 
him by Government. 

Note. —Persons who migrated to India from 'Pakistan before 19th July 1948 and 
have ordinarily been resident in India since then are eligible for appointment to 
services and posts under the Government of India without certificates of eligibility 
qua citizens of India. Persons who so migrated on or after the 19th July 1948 are 
non-citizens and must secure certificates of eligibility for appointment to Union 
Services, unless they had migrated before 3()th September 1948 and had got themselves 
registered us citizens within the time allowed. 

6. Candidates should be medically fit in all respect*. The standards of medical 
fitness are shown in Appendix i. 

Parents /Guardians of candidates must arrange themselves the medical examination 
of their sons/ wards by u Government Medical Officer not below the rank of Civil 
Surgeon. The medical examination report of the candidate must be submitted along 
with the application. 


7. Parents /Guardians ot candidates must undertake that their sons/ wards will 

not marry whilst at the College and until be has completed, subsequently, a course at 
the National Defence Academy, or the corresponding course for the Air Force or the 
Navy. A candidate who marries subsequent to the date of his application, though 
successful at the ensuing or any subsequent examination will not be selected for training 
ami a candidate who marries while under training shall be discharged and will be 
liable to refund all expenditure incurred on him by the Government. i 

8. No educational qualification is prescribed for admission to this College but it is 

expected that the candidate should have rcud up to Glass VJi standard of a Secondary 
School. As all instructions in this College are given through the medium of English, 
the candidate must be able to read, write and speak English freely. He must have 
good general knowledge ot all current topics and must be smart and have sound cum- 
monsense and intelligence. . • 


9, The candidate must satisfy the State Government and the Principal of the 
(allege that he is suitable in all respects for admission to the College. 


10. The decision of the State Government as to the eligibility or otherwise of a 
candidate shall be final. 

11. No candidal# shall be admitted to the examination unless he holds a certi- 
ficate or admission from the Rome (Defence) Department, ^Government of West Bengal. 

12. 1 he maximum uumlwr ol candidates U> be admitted to the examination may 
at the discretion of the Government of India be limited to such number as the Gov- 
ernment m India may decide, li a limit is imposed and the number of candidates 
exceeds that limit, the State Government shall select from among the candidates those 
W i R T l i * , nutted to the examination and shall have regard in so doing to the 
suitability of the applicants for admission to the College.

APPENDIX I. 

Physical condition for admission to the Prince of Wales's Military College, Dehra Dun. 

1. To be passed as fit for admission to the Prince of Wales’s Military College, a 
candidate must be in good mental and bodily health, and free from any physical detect 
likely to interfere with the efficient performance of military duty. 

2. A standard for height, and chest measurement and physical development cannot 
he laid down, hut the candidate should not he below the average for his ago and race. 

3 Tho candidate’s height will he measured as follows: — 

He will he placed against the standard with his feet together, and the weight 
thrown on the heels and not cm the toes or outer sides of the feet. Ho will stand 
erect, without rigidity and with the heels, calves, buttocks and shoulders touching the 
standard; the chill will depressed to bring the vertex of the head level under the 

horizontal bar, and the height will be recorded in inches and parts of an inch to 

quarters. 

4. The candidate’s chest will he measured ns follows: — 

He will he made to stand erect with Ins feet together, and to raise his arms over 

his head. The tape will he so adjusted round the chest that its upper edge touches 

the inferior angles of the shoulder-blades behind, and its low«r edge the upper part 
of the nipples in front. The arms will then lie lowered to hang loosely by the side, 
and care will. he taken that the shoulders are not thrown upwards or backwards so as to 
displace the tape. The candidate will then be directed to take a deep inspiration 
several times, and the maximum expansion of the chest will be carefully noted. The 
minimum and muximum will then be recorded. In recording the measurements, 
fractions of less than half an inch should not he noted. 

5. The candidate will also be weighed, and his weight recorded in pounds Frac- 
tions of a pound should not be noted. 

6. The examination for determining the acuteness of vision includes two tests; one 
for distant, tho other for near vision. The Snellen’s .type should be used for tho tost 
for distant vision, without glasses at a distance of 20 feot, and for tho test for near 
vision withmit glasses, at any distance selected hy the candidate. The standards of 
the minimum acuteness of vision with which a candidate will he considered fit arc: - - 


Better eye. Worse eye. 

Distant vision — V-6/6. Distant vision not below 6/ Of). 

After correction with glasses not below 0/18. 
Near vision reads 0‘6. • Near vision reads 0 6 


Each eye must have a full field of vision as tested by hand movements. 

Squint or any morbid condition of tho eyes or of tho lid of either eye liable to the 
risk of aggravation or recurrence will cause rejection of the candidate. 

Each eye will ho examined separately. The candidate will he required to read the 
tests in ordinary daylight. % 

Inability to distinguish the,, principal colours will not be regarded as cause for 
rejection but the fact will be noted in the proceedings and the candidate informed. 

No relaxation of the standard of vision will bo allowed.

(а) * That his hearing is good. (The ears should be examined internally with an 

auroseope.)’ 

(б) That his speech is without impediment. 

(c) That his teeth are in good order. He must have 10 sound teeth in the upper 
jaw functionally opposed to 10 sound teeth in the lower jaw. Two of these 
teeth in each jaw must be molars. Well filled teeth wifi be considered as 
sound. 


(d) That his chest is well formed and that his lungs and heart are sound. 

(r) That he is not ruptured. 

(J) That he does not suffer from a severe degree of varicocele* or varicose veins.

Sales Office at Writers* Buildings up to 12 noon on Saturday and at Head Office at Alipore up to 12 noon on Monday.

(PUBLICATION BRANCH), WE8T BENGAL GOVERNMENT PRE88, ALIPORE.

Advertisement No. 92(e). 

A PPLICATIONS are invited for a temporary post of 
Rationing Officer (non -gazetted) in tho Directorate of 
Rationing and Distribution, West Bengal. 

The selected candidate will he liable for service in any 
post analogous to the rank of Rationing Officer under the 
Food, Relief and Supplies Department of the Government 
of West Bengal anywhere in the State on the same salary 
and allowance. 

Tho candidate selected for the post will be required to 
produce a medical certificate of fitness from a medical 
officer not below the rank of a Civil Surgeon. 

(1 ) Qualifications. — 

(i) Citizenship of India us defined in Part II of the 
Constitution of India. 

(ii) A degree of a recognised University. 

(iii) Administrative experience. 

(iv) Ability to exercise disciplinary control over 

subordinates. • 

(v) Ability to read, write and speak Bengali. 

(vi) Age between 25 and 40 years on 1st August 1953, 
the upper limit being relaxable for a candidate 
in Government service. 

I'he upper age limit is relaxable for a non-Muslim Gov- 
ernment servant in undivided Bengal who had originally 
opted to served in Fast Bengal and wan working under 
the Government of Fast Bengal after partition but has 
since formally resigned his service under that Govern- 
ment and has come over to India as refugee. 

A candidate who before the lJth August 1947 was 
detained, imprisoned, interned or externed on account of 
his activities in connection with the country’s strugglo for 
independence, not being convicted of an ofFoneo, indicat- 
ing moral turpitude, shall ho entitled to a concession in 
respect of the upper age limit. The concession granted 
will be equal to the exact period of detention, imprison- 
ment, internment or oxternmont suffered up to a maxi- 
mum of four years. 

(2) Pay. —The post carries a fixed pay of Rs. 300 plus 

the usual allowances. • 

(3) instructions regarding submission of applications.— 

Applications are to be made on the prescribed form (West 
Bengal Form No. 909) whieh has been made saleable and 
priced annas two per copy to mako it readily available to •

Fi rn ploy men t Exchange, Calcutta, may obtain the form from 
that, office. Persons residing outside West Bengal may 
obtain the form from the office of the Commission on 
sending the price of the form in stamps of denomination of 
six pies only. A large self-addressed envelope with stamps, 
sufficient to cover the postage affixed to it, must accom- 
pany every request for the supply of the form Candidates 
who are unable to obtain copies of the prescribed form may

IN accordance with the provisions of sob-section (4) of 
section 120 of the Calcutta Port Act, 1890 (Bengal Act III

Commissioners propose to incorporate in the by-laws for 
the Port of Calcutta, subject to the confirmation of the 
Government of India, is hereby published for general 
information: — 

Proposed new by-law No. itOA. 

“No jwrson shall take photographs, movies or pictorial 
representation of any other kind whatsoever of 
or in the Docks, .Jetties and other properties of 
tho Commissioners without a written permit from 
the Secretary first had and obtained. Such 
permit, if granted, shall bo subject, to such condi- 
tions as mar he laid down therein. The grant 
for refusal of such permit shall he at tho discretion 
of tho Secretary whoso decision shall he final.” 

The proposed by-law will he submitted to the Govern 
mont of India for confirmation on the expiry of fourteen 
days after the first publication of this notification in the 
State Gazette and comments oi criticisms if any with 
regard thereto are invited.

APPLICATIONS are invited for a permanent post of 
Health Officer, Corporation of Calcutta. The selected 
candidate will he required to supervise the Motor Ambulance 
Service of the Corporation. The service will be terminable 
>n six months’ notice on either side. He shall be on pro- 
bation tor one year. He will be required to submit to 
nodical examination before' taking up his appointment and 
U) join within one month ot receiving the notice of 
ippointment. 

(1) Qualifications. — 

(») Citizenship ol India as defined in Part II of the 
Constitution of Tnrlia. ■* 

(u) A degree in medicine. 

(iii) A degree or diploma in Sanitary Science', Public 
Health or State Medicine. 

(iv> Five wars' experience as n Sanitarian or Health 
Officer ot a eitv with a population ol at least one 
lakh. 

(v) Administrative experience. 

(vi) Age not more than 50 years on 1st September 
1953, relaxable for a person already in the service 
of Calcutta Corporation. 

(2) Pay. — The scale of pay is Rs. 1,000 — 50 — 1,500 plus 
a motor car allowance of Rs. 150 per month. The selected 
candidate will not he allowed to take lip any outside work 
whether carrying any emolument or not, without previous 
sanction of the Corporation, or engage in private practice. 
The appointment is subject to the Provident Fund, Leavo 
and other sen ices rules of the Corporation. At present 
-*1 per cent, ol the salary is deducted every month us con- 
tribution to the Provident Fund and an equivalent amount 
is contributed by the Corporation at • the end ot the year 
which is crcniited to the subscriber’s account. The fund 
accumulates at compound interest. The person appointed 
will be required to keep a motor car. The cost of the 
motor ear will, if desired, be advanced by the Corporation 
and recovered with interest according to the Government 
rate in monthly instalments spreading over three years. 

(3) instruction! regarding submission of applications.— 

Applications are to be made on the prescribed form (West 
Bengal Form No. 969) which has been made saleable and 
priced annas two per copy to make it readily available to 
candidates. It will be available on payment from the 
allowing places: — Office of the Public Service Commission, 
West Bengal, Anderson House (ground floor), Alipore, 
Calcutta-27, all District Treasuries and Sub-Treasuries in 
West Bengal, the Sales Depot of the Publication Branch. 
Writers’ Buildings, Calcutta. Persons registered at the 
Employment Exchange, Calcutta, may obtain the form from 
x bat office. Persons residing outside West Bengal may 
®btam the form from the office of the Commission on 
•ending the price of the form in stamps of denomination 


of six pies only. A largo self-addressed envelope with 
stamps, sufficient to cover the postage affixed to it. must 
accompany every request for the supply of the term. 
Candidates who are unable to obtain copies ot the pres- 
cribed form may apply on any similar typed (not hand- 
written) form, showing exactly the wording aud spacing of 
the sample form published in the “Calcutta Gnrcttc” of 
the 10th March 1949, provided the blanks tire filled up 
in the candidates’ own handwriting. 

The applications must be addressed to the Secretary 
and should reach him not later than the 5th September 
1953. 

(4) Partloulart and certificates required. —Candidates 
should furnish evidence of their age, qualifications and 
previous experience together with certificates written not 
more than one year prior to the date of their applications, 
from responsible persons, testifying to their private 
character. Relationship, if any, with the Mayor, Coun- 
cillors, Aldermen and the Officers ot the Corporation, should 
be stated. 

(5) Fee. — Candidates must enclose with their applications 
a fee of Rs. 5 in the form of a receipts! rhalan 
from a Government Treasury or the Reset ve Hank 
of Lidia umb*r the head “XXX VI Miscellaneous— 
Receipts of the Public Servieo Commission, West 
Bengal”. Money orders, cheques, etc., in lieu of 
Treasury chalans are not accepted. Postal orders, however, 
may be accepted ttom candidates. They should he crossed 
and made payable to “the Secretary, Public Service Com- 
mission, West Bengal”. No application will be considered 
unless accompanied with the requisite application fee. 

Candidates in Government service should make sure 
before depositing fee that their applications will he for- 
warded by their superior officers. In no ease will the fee 
paid with the application he refunded. 

(6) Address . — Candidates should give their present 
address and should communicate at once any subsequent 
change of address. 

(7) Canvassing. — Any attempt on the part of candidates 
to enlist support of their applications through persons of 
influence or officials of Government will disqualify them 
for appointment. Spontaneous recommendation' from 
persons interested in the candidates or otherwise known 
to them will be disregarded. 

(8) Applications irom candidates who are in permanent

PART II — Advertisements, Notices 

Procedure regarding sending Manuscripts for publication of Advertisements, Notices, «tc., in 

the "Calcutta Gazette" (Part II). 

1. Manuscripts should be properly edited and complete In Itself. 

2. Manuscripts should always be typewritten on one side of the paper. The name of the signatory should be type- 
written below the signature. 

3. Manuscripts Intended for advertisement In the next issue of “Calcutta Gazette" shall be reoeived by Publication 
Sales Office at Writers' Buildings up to 12 noon on Saturday and at Head Offkoe at Allpore up to 12 noon on Monday. 

4. All costs shall be paid In advance and deposited along with the Manuscripts. 

5. Manuscripts and postal remittanoes shall be addressed to SUPERINTENDENT, GOVERNMENT PRINTING 
(PUBLICATION BRANCH), WEST BENGAL GOVERNMENT PRE88, ALIPORE. 

The Press shall not be heir responsible "for delay in publication of any advertisement due to the non-observance of the 
instructions detailed above.

PART II — Advertisements, Notices 

Procedure regarding sending Manuscripts for publication of Advertisements, Notices, etc., in 

the “Calcutta Gazette” 1 (Part IK). 

1. Manuscripts should be properly edited and complete In itself. 

2. Manuscripts should always be typewritten on one side of the paper. The name of the signatory should be type- 
ritten below the signature. 

3. Manuscripts Intended for advertisement In the next issue of “Calcutta Gazette" shall be received by Publication 
Hies Office at Writers' Buildings up to 12 noon on Saturday and at Head Office at Alipore up to 12 noon on Monday. 

4. All costs shall be paid In advance and deposited afong with tho Manuscripts. 

5. Manuscripts and postal remittances Shall be addressed to SUPERINTENDENT, GOVERNMENT PRINTING 
PUBLICATION BRANCH), WEST BENGAL GOVERNMENT PRE88, ALIPORE. 

The Press shall not be held responsible for delay in publication of any advertisement due to the non-observance of the 
structlon8 detailed above.

PART II — Advertisements, Notices 

Procedure regarding sending Manuscripts for publication of Advertisements, Notioes, etc., in 

the “Calcutta Gazette” (Part II). 

1. Manuscripts should bo properly edited and complete ;n itself. 

2. Manuscripts should always be typewritten on one side ot the paper. The namo of the signatory should be type- 

written below the signature. 

3. Manuscripts intended for advertisement In the next issue of “Calcutta Gazette” shall be received by Publication 
Sales Office at Writers’ Buildings up to 12 noon on Saturday and at Head Office at Alipore up to 12 noon on Monday. 

4 . All costs shall be paid In advance and deposited along with the Manuscripts. 

5 Manuscripts and postal remittances shall be addressed to SUPERINTENDENT, GOVERNMENT PRINTING 

'UBLI CATION BRANCH), WE8T BENGAL GOVERNMENT PRESS, ALIPORE. 

The Press shall not bo held responsible for delay In publication of any advertisement due to the non-observanco of the 
structions detailed above.

the “Calcutta Gazette” (Part II). 


1. Manuscripts should bo properly edited and oomplete In Itself.

written below the signature.

Sales Office at Writers' Buildings up to 12 noon on Saturday and at Head Office at Allpore up to 12 noon on Monday. 


s. All costs shall be paid in advanoe and deposited along with the Manuscripts.

following places:-- Office of the Public Service Commission,

from a Government. Treasury or the Deserve Bank

Bengal’*. Money orders, cheques, etc:., in lieu of Treasury

reserihed fee should forward along with his application

ficate (also in original) from a District Officer or a Gazetted

For the purpose of the concessions referred to above the 
definition of “Displaced person” will be as follows: — 

Definition. — “Displaced person” means a person ordi- 
narily resident in the territories now comprising 
Eastern Pakistan or being a Bengalee in the terri- 
tories now comprising other parts of Pakistan or 
in an Indian State which is not an Acceding State 
who has, since the 1st day of June 1947 arrived 
from the said territories or State in a place in 
West Bengal on account of civil disturbances or 
fear of such disturbances or the partition of India 
and intends to take up his permanent residence in 
the State of West Bengal in the Union of India: 

Provided that in the case of persona ordinarily resident 
in the district of Noakhali or Tippera, the time of 
leaving such residence shall run from the 1st day 
of October 1946. 

Note. — Persons falling within these categories will not bo 
entitled to such concessions if they have already been in 
permanent service under Government. 

(6) Address. — Candidates should give their present 
address and should communicate at once any subsequent 
change of address. 

(7) Canvassing. — Anv attempt on the part of candidates 
to enlist support of their applications through persons of 
influence or officials of Government will disqualify them for 
appointment. Spontaneous recommendation from persons 
interested in the candidates or otherwise known to them 
will be disregarded. 

• 

(8) Applications from candidates who are in permanent 
or temporary employment under any Government, a local 
or Statutory Body (e.g., Damod'ar Valley Corporation), in 
India will ho rejected unlesR they are submitted through 
the appointing authority of their posts or service.

PART II — Advertisements, Notices 

Procedure regarding sending Manuscripts for publication of Advertisements, Notices, etc., in 

the “Calcutta Gazette” (Part II). 

1. Manuscripts should be properly edited and complete in Itself. 

2. Manuscripts should always be typewritten on one side of the paper. The name of the signatory should be type* 
ntten below the signature. 

3 . Manuscripts intended for advertisement in the next issue of “ Calcutta Gazette" shall be received by Publication 
ties Office at Writers* Buildings up to 12 noon on Saturday and at Head Qffioe at Allpore up to 12 noon on Monday. 

4 . All costs shall be paid In advance and deposited along with the Manuscripts. 

5 Manuscripts and postal remittances shall be addressed to SUPERINTENDENT, GOVERNMENT PRINTING 
’UBLI CATION BRANCH), WEST BENGAL GOVERNMENT PRESS, ALIPORE. 

The Pr ess shall not be held responsible for delay in publication of any advertisement due to the non-observance of the 
iifructions derailed above.

ACT NO. XXIII OF 1953. 

1H1 INDIAN MERCHANT SHIPPING (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1953. 

[21st May, 1953.] 

» 

I ,| i ( / /<> amble t'ffci t to be given to an International Convention for the Safety 
<»! / tje at Sea, signed in London on the tenth day of June, nineteen hundred 
and lorty-eight, to amend the ptovisions of the Indian Merchant Shipping 
Ait, 1923 relating to lifesaving appliances, wireless and radio navigational 
aid. and to other matters affected by the said Convention. 

Bi u enacted by Parliament as follows: — 

1. Short title and commencement. — (I) This* Act may be called the Indian 
Merchant Shipping (Amendment) Act, 1953. 

13) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, 
notification in the Official Gazette, appoint 

2. Substitution of certain expressions for certain other expressions in Act 
\\I of 1923. — In the Indian Merchant Shipping Act, 1923 (hereinafter referred 
i" the principal Act), except as otherwise provided in this Act.-— 

(a) in Part V and in clause ()) ol section 2X0, for the words ‘wiriless 
telegraphy inspectors’ and ‘wireless telegraphy inspector’ wherever 
they occur, the words ‘radio inspectors’ and ‘radio inspector’ shall, 
respectively, be substituted; 

((>) In Part V, — 

</) lor the words and figures ‘International Convention respecting Load 
Lines, 1930* wherever they occur, the words ‘Load Line Con- 
vention’ shall be substituted;

(//) for the words and figures ‘International Convention for the Safety 
' of Life at Sea, 1929’. or ‘International Convention for the Safety 
of Life at Sea signed* in London on the 31st day of May, 1929 *' 
wherever they occur, the words ‘Safety Convention’ shall be 
substituted; 

(Hi) for the word ‘wireless’ wherever it occurs, the word ‘radio’ shall 
be substituted; 

(/v) after the words ‘telegraph’ and ‘telegraphy’ wherever they occur 
the words ‘or radio-telephone’ and ‘or radio-telephony’ shall, 
respectively, be inserted. 

3. Amendment of section 2, Act XXI of 1923.— -In section 2 of the prin- 
cipal Act, for clause (6), the following clause shall be substituted, namely:— 

“(6) ‘passenger’ means any person carried in a ship, except — 

(a) a person employed or engaged in any capacity on board the ship 

on the business of the ship; 

( b ) a person on board the ship either in pursuance of the obligation 

laid upon the .master to carry ship-wrecked, distressed or other 
persons, or by reasons of any circumstances which neither the 
master nor the charterer, if any, could have prevented or fore- 
stalled; and 

(c) a child under one year of age.” 


4. Omission of section 143A, Act XXI of 1923. — Section 143 A of the 
principal Act shall be omitted. 

5. Amendment of section 145A, Act XXI of 1923. — In section 145A ol 
the principal Act, in sub-section (2), for clauses (a) to (h), the following 
clauses shall be substituted, namely: — 

“(a) the closing and keeping closed the openings in steamers’ hulls anc 
. in water-tight bulk-heads; 

(/») the securing of, and keeping in place and inspecting contrivance' 
for closing any such openings as aforesaid; 

(r) the operation of mechanisms of contrivances for closing any such 
openings as aforesaid and the drills in connection with the opera 
tion thereof; and 

(d) the entries to be n\ade in the Official Log Book or other record ic 
be kept of any of the matters aforesaid.” 

6. Substitution of new section for section 21 3 A in Act XXI of 1923. — toi 

section 213A of the principal Act, the following section shall be substituted 
namely: — 

“213A. Definitions. — In this Part, unless the context otherwise requires - 

(a) ‘country to which the Load Line Convention applies’ means— 

(/) a country the Government of which has been declared or is deemed 
to have been declared under section 213B to have accepted the 
Load Line Convention and has not been so declared to have 
denounced that Convention; 

(//) a country to which it has been so declared that the Load l ine 
Convention has been applied under the provisions of article 
twenty-one thereof, not being a country to which it has been w 
declared that that Convention has ceased to apply under the 
provisions of that article;

(/,) ‘country to which the Safety Convention applies’ means- 


d) a country the Government of which has been declared under section 
213B to have accepted the Safety Convention and has not been 
so declared to have denounced that Convention; 


in) a territory to which it has been so declared that the Safety Conven- 
' tion extends, not being a territory to which it has been so declared

(t) ‘Load Line Convention’ means the Convention signed in London on 
the fifth day of July, nineteen hundred and thirty, for promoting

( t /) ‘Safety Convention’ means the Convention for the Safety of Life at 
Sea, signed in London on the tenth day of June, nineteen hundred 
and forty-eight, as amended from time to time.” 


7. Insertion of new section 213B in Act XXI of 1923. — After section 213A 
of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted, namely: — 

”2 1 3B. Countries to which Load Line Convention or Sajety Convention 
applies - -( 7 ) The Central Government, if satisfied, — 

(a) that the Government of any country has accepted or denounced the 
Load Line Convention or, as the case may be, the Safety Con- 
vention; or 

(/>) that the Load Line Convention or, as the case may be, the Safety 
Convention extends, or has ceased to extend to any territory; 


mav. by notification in the Official Gazette, make a declaration to that effect. 

( - ) Any declaration made by or on behalf of the Central Government before 
the commencement of the Indian Merchant Shipping (Amendment) Act, 1953, 
m any form whatsoever, that the Government of any country has accepted or 
denounced the Load Line Convention or that the said Convention extends or 
has ceased to extend to any territory shall be deemed to have been made under 
sub-section (7).” 


8. Amendment of sections 214 and 216, Act XXI of 1923. — In sub- 
section (!) of section 214 and in section 216 of the principal Act, after the 
word “lights” the words “and shapes” shall be inserted. 


9. Amendment of section 216A, Act XXI of 1923. — In section 216A of 
the principal Act, after sub-section (7), the following sub-section shall be 
inserted, namely: — 


“(7A) Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing provision, such 
rules may provide for all or any of the following matters, namely: — 

(a) the arranging of ships into classes, having regard to the services in 

which they are employed, to the nature and duration of the voyage 
and to the number of persons carried; 

(b) the number, description and mode, of construction of the boats, life 

rafts, line throwing appliances, life-jackets and life-buoys to be 
carried by ships according to the classes in which the ships are 
♦ arranged; 

(r) the equipment to be carried by any such boats and rafts and the method 
to be provided to get the boats and other life-saving appliances into 
the water, including oil for use in stormy weather; 

(</) the provision in ships of a proper supply of lights inextinguishable 
in water and fitted for attachment to life-buoys; 



ft’) the quantity, quality and description of buoyant apparatus to be carjfe 
on board ships either in addition to or in substitution for boats 
life rafts, life-jackets and life-buoys; 

(/) the position and means of securing the boats, life rafts, life-jackeu 
life-buoys and buoyant apparatus; 

(g) the marking of boats, life rafts, and buoyant apparatus so as to shot 

their dimensions and the number of persons authorised to be carrie 
on them; 

(h) the manning of lifeboats and the qualifications and certificates of ]j[ e 

boatmen; 

(/) the provision to be made for mustering the persons on board and fo 
embarking them in the boats (including provision for the lightim 
of, and the means of ingress and egress from, different parts of thi 
ship); 

(/') the provision of suitable means situated outside the engine-room whereto 
any discharge of water into the boats can be prevented; 

( k ) the assignment of specific duties to each member of the crew in cas< 
of emergency; 

(/) the methods to be adopted and the appliances to be carried in ship 
for the prevention, detection and extinction of fire; 

(m) the practice in ships of boat-drills and fire-drills; 

( n ) the provision in ships of means of making effective distress signals b\ 

day and by night; 

(t>) the provision in ships, engaged on voyages in which pilots arc likeh 
to be embarked of suitable pilot ladders, and of ropes, lights and 
other appliances designed to make the use of such ladders safe; and 

( p ) the periodical examination of any appliances or equipment required 
by any rules made under this Act to be carried by ships.” 

10. Substitution of new sections for sections 225 and 226 in Act XXI oj 
1923. — For sections 225 and 226 and the heading thereto, the following shall 
be substituted, namely: — 

"Dangerous Goods and Grain-Cargoes. 

225. Carriage of dangerous goods. — (/) The Central Government ma\ 
make rules for regulating in the interests of safety the carriage of dangerous 
goods in ships to which this section applies. 

(2) This section applies to — 

(а) Indian ships; 

(б) other ships while they are within any port in India or arc embarking 

or disembarking passengers within the territorial waters of India, or 
are loading or discharging cargo or fuel within those waters. 

(3) If any of the rules made in pursuance of this section is not complied with 
in relation to any ship, the owner or master of the ship shall be liable to a line 
which may extend to three thousand rupees and the ship shall be deemed lor 
the purpose of this Part to be an unsafe ship. 

226. Carriage of grain. — (/) Where grain is loaded on board any Indian 
ship or is loaded within any port in India on board any ship, all necessary and 
reasonable precautions shall be taken to prevent the grain from shifting; and if 
such precautions as aforesaid arc not taken, the owner or the master of the 
ship or any agent of the owner who was charged with the loading or with sending 
the ship to sea laden with grain shall be guilty of an offence under this sub- 
section and the ship shall be deemed for the purposes of this Part to be unsafe 
by reason of improper loading. 



l>\,rr V] THE CALC ETTA GAZETTE, JULY 2, 19b;t 


127 


* (2) Where any ship which is loaded with grain outside India without all 

necessary and reasonable precautions having been taken to prevent the grain 
Ironi shifting, enters any port in India so laden, the owner or master of the 
ship shall be guilty of an offence under this sub-section and the ship shall be 
deemed for the purposed of this Part to be unsafe by reason of improper loading: 

Provided that this sub-section shall not have effect if the ship would not 
have entered any such port but* for stress of weather or any other circumstance 
that neither the master nor the owner nor the charterer, if any, could have pre- 
vented or forestalled. 


(.?) If any person commits an offence under sub-section (7) or sub-section 
he shall be liable to a fine which may extend to three thousand rupees. 

(*/) On the arrival at a port in India from a port outside India of any ship 

carrying a cargo of grain, the master shall cause to be delivered at the port to 
such customs or other officer as may be specified by the Central Government 
in this behalf, a notice stating — 

(a) the draught ot water and free-board of the said ship after the loading 

of the cargo was completed at the final port of loading; and 

(b) the following particulars of the grain carried, namely: — 

(/) the kind of grain and quantity thereof stated in cubic feet, quarters 
bushels or tons weight; ’ 

(if) thc mode «n which the grain is stowed; and

19 . Amendment of section 35, Act XI of 1922. — In section 35 of the 
principal Act, after sub-section (4), the following sub-sections shall be inserted, 
namely : — 

“(5) Where in respect of any completed assessment of a partner in a firm 
j t is found on the assessment or re-assessment of the firm or on any reduction 
or enhancement made in the income of the firm under section 31, section 33, 
section 33A, section 33B, section 66 or section 66A that the share of the 
partner in the profit or loss of the firm has not been included in the assessment 
of the partner or, if included, is not correct, the inclusion of the share in the 
assessment or the correction thereof, as the case may be, shall be deemed to 
he a rectification of a mistake apparent from the record within the meaning of 
this section, and the provisions of sub-section (7 ) shall apply thereto accord- 
ingly, the period of four years referred to in that sub-section being computed from 
the date of the final order passed in the case of the firm. 

(6) Where the excess profits tax or the business profits tax payable by an 
assessee has been modified in appeal, revision or any other proceeding, or 
where any excess profits tax or business profits tax has been assessed after the 
completion of the corresponding assessment for income-tax [whether before or 
after the commencement of the Indian Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1953j 
and in consequence thereof it is necessary to re-compute the total income of the 
assessee chargeable to income-tax, such re-computation shall be deemed to be a 
rectification of a mistake apparent from the record within the meaning of this 
section, and the provisions of sub-section (/) shall apply accordingly, the 
period of four years, referred to in that sub-section being computed from the 
date of the order making or modifying the assessment of such excess profits tax

18D. No right to compensation for termination of offence or contract , — 
Notwithstanding anything contained in any law’ for the time being in force, no

his contract of management : 


Provided that nothing contained in this section shall affect the right of any 
such person to recover from the industrial undertaking moneys recoverable 
otherwise than by way of such compensation. 

18E. Application of Act VII of 1913.— (7) Where the management of an

except with the consent of the Central Government.

of 1913), shall continue to apply to such undertaking in the same manner as it 
applied thereto before the issue of the notified order under section 18 A. 


18F. Power of Central Government to cancel notified order under section 

18 A. If at any time it appears to the Central Government on the application 

of the owner of the industrial undertaking or otherwise that the purpose of the 
order made under section 18A has been fulfilled or that for any other reason 
it is not necessary that the order should remain in forces, the Central Govern- 
ment may, by notified order, cancel such order and on the cancellation of any 
such order the management or the control, as the-casc may be, of the industrial 
undertaking shall vest in the owner of the undertaking.

CHAPTER II 


The Tea Board 

4 . Establishment and constitution of the Tea Board.— ( 7 ) With effect 
from "urli det® as tdie Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, specify in this behalf, there shall be established for the 
purposes of this Act a Board to be called the Tea Board. 

(i!) The Board shall be a body corporate by the name aforesaid, having 
perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold and 
dispose of property, both movable and immovable, and to contract, and 
shall by the said name sue and be sued. 


(/I) The Board shall consist of a Chairman and such number of other 
members not exceeding forty as the Central Government may think 
expedient, to be appointed by that Government by notification in the 
Official Gazette from among persons who are in its opinion capable of 

representing, — 

(a) owners of tea estates and gardens and growers of tea; 

(In persons employed in tea estates and gardens; 

(r) manufacturers of tea; 

(il) dealers including both exporters and internal traders of tea; 

(c) consumers; 

(/) Parliament; 

(</) the Governments of the principal tea growing States; 

(h) such other persons or class of persons, who, in the opinion of the 
Central Government, ought to be represented on the Board. 


(4) The number of persons to be appointed as members from each of 
the categories specified in sub-section (.j), the term of office of, the pro- 
cedure to be followed in the discharge of their functions by, and the 
maimer of filling vacancies among, the members of the Board sliall be such 
as may he prescribed. 


(o) Any officer of the Central Government when deputed by that Gov- 
ernment in this behalf shall have the right to attend meetings of the Board 
and take part in the proceedings thereof but shall not be entitled to vote. 


:>. Vacancies, etc., not to invalidate acts and proceedings.— No act done 
or proceeding taken by the Board under this Act shall lie questioned on 
the giound merely of the existence of any vacancy in, or defect iu the 
constitution of, the Board. 

ti. Salary and allowances of Chairman. — The Chairman shall be entitled 
to sm h salary and allowances and such conditions of service in respect of 
leave, pension, provident fund and other matters as may from time to time 
be fixed by the Central Government. 

7. Vice-Chairman. — The Board shall elect from among its members a 
’ ice-Clmirman who shall exercise such of the powers and discharge ,.ueh 
°1 the duties of the Chairman as may be prescribed or as may be delegated 
to him by the Chairman.

(.?) The Chairman, Secretary and other employees of the Board shall

10. Functions Of the Board. — (71 It shall be the duty of the Board to 
promote, by such measures as it thinks fit, the development under the 
control of the Central Government of the tea industry. 


(2) Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions of sub-section 
(7), the measures referred to therein may provide for — 

(a) regulating the production and extent of cultivation of tea : 

(h) improving the quality of tea ; 

(c) promoting co-operative efforts among growers and manufacturers 

of tea; 

(d) undertaking, assisting or encouraging scientific, technological nu<l 

economic research aud maintaining or assisting in the 
maintenance, of demonstration farms and manufacturing stations; 

^c) assisting in the control of insects and other pests and 1 1 i<(*;ises 
affecting tea ; 

(/) regulating the sale and export of tea ; 

(g) training in tea tasting and fixing gi>ade standards of tea ;

Tlu' following Act of. the Parliament of India received the assent of the 
President on the 6th October 1953 and is hereby published for general 
inhumation : — 

ACT No. XXXIV OF 1953. 

THE ESTATE DUTY ACT, 1953. 

[6th October, 1663. ] 

An Act to provide for the levy and collection of an estate duty. 

Uk it enacted by Parliament as follows: — 

PART 1. — Pkeliminaih . 

1, Short title, extent and commencement.— (1 > This Act may be called 
tbe Estate Duty Act, 1953. 

(2) it extends to the whole ol India except the State of Jammu and 
Ka-hinir. 

(3 > It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government 
in, a . by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint. 

2. Definitions. — In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires, — 

(1) “affidavit of valuation” means the affidavit of valuation made 
under section 19-1 of the Court -fees Act, 1870 (Y1J of 1870), in 
connection with an application lor the grant of representation; 

»2) “Board” means the -Central Board of Revenue constituted under 
the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1924 (TV of 1924); 

(-3) “company” includes anybody corporate wheresoever incorporated; 

(4) “controlled company” means a company as defined in section 17; 

(5) “Controller” means a person appointed to be a Controller of 

Estate Duty tinder section 4 and includes a person appointed to 
be a Deputy Controller of Estate Duty or an Assistant, Controller 
of Estate Duty; 

(ti) deceased person” and “the deceased” mean a person dying after 
tbe commencement of this Act;

(11) “interest in expectancy” includes an estate in remainder

(12) “legal representative” means a person who in law represents t|

3. Interpretation. — (1) For the purposes of this Act, — 

(a) a person shall be deemed competent to dispose of property if be has 

such an estate or interest therein or such general power as would, 

if he were sui juris , enable him to dispose of the property; 

(b) a disposition taking effect out of the interest of the deceased shall 

be deemed to have been made by him, whether the concurrence 
of any other person was or was not required; 

(c) money which a person has a general power to charge on the property 

of another person shall be deemed to be an interest in that pro- 
perty of which the former has power to dispose; 

(d) the domicile of a person shall be determined as if the provisions 

of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 (XXXIX of 1925), on the 
subject applied to him. 

(2) In Parts II and III of this Act, any reference to any interest dis- 
posed of, policy of insurance effected, annuity or other interest purchased 
or provided or to any gift, settlement, disposition or transfer of property 
made, shall be construed as including any such interest, policy, annuity, 
gift, settlement, disposition or transfer, as the case may be, whether it was 
disposed of, effected, purchased or provided, or made before or after the 
coimnencement of this Act. 

4. Estate duty authorities. — (1) There shall be the following authori- 
ties for the purposes of this Act, namely: — 

(a) the Board, 

(L) Controllers of Estate Duty, 

i<‘) Valuers.

Duty as it thinks fit and they shall, subject to the control of the Board, 
perform their functions in respect of such estates or classes of estates and 
such areas as are assigned to them by the Board :

Controller by this Act :

other Controller.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA. 

Ministry of Law. 

Ordinance No. I of 1953. 

HE EMPLOYEES’ PROVIDENT FUNDS (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 

1953. 

An Ordinance to amend the Employees’ Provident Funds Act, 1952. 

Whereas a Bill to amend the Employees' Provident Funds Act has been 
troduced in Parliament but has not yet been passed; 

And whereas Parliament is not in session and the President is satisfied that 
rcunistances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action 
give effect to some of the amendments proposed in the said Bill; 

Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by clause (1) of 
tide 1 23 of the Constitution, the President is pleased to promulgate the follow- 
g Ordinance : — 

1. Short title and commencement. — (1) This Ordinance may be called the 
inplovces’ Provident Funds (Amendment) Ordinance, 1953. 

(3) It shall come into force at once. 

2. Amendment of section 2, Act XIX of 1952. — In section 2 of the 
mployees’ Provident Funds Act, 1952 (hereinafter referred to as the principal 
ct), after clause (/), the following clause shall be inserted, namely : — 

"(id) ‘manufacture’ means making, altering, ornamenting, finishing or other- 
wise treating or adapting any article or substance with a view to its 
use, sale, transport, delivery or disposal;”. 

3. Amendment of section 5, Act XIX of 1952. — Section 5 of the principal 
ct shall be renumbered as sub-section (1) thereof and after sub-section (/) as so 
numbered, the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely : — 

"(2) A Scheme framed under sub-section (/) may provide that any of its 
provisions shall take effect cither prospectively or retrospectively 
with effect from such date as may be specified in this behalf in the 
Scheme.” 

4. Amendment of section 13, Act XIX of 1952. — In sub-section (?) of 
ction 13 of the principal Act, — 

(a) after the words “have been complied with”, the following shall be 
inserted, namely : — 

“in respect of a factory to which any Scheme applies or for the purpose 
of ascertaining whether the provisions of this Act or any Scheme 
are applicable to any factory to which the Scheme has not been 
applied or for the purpose of determining whether the conditions 
subject to which exemption was granted under section 1 7 are being 
complied with, — 

(/>) in clause (a), the words “in relation to the Scheme” shall be omitted. 

5. Amendment of section 14, Act XIX of 1952. — In section 14 of the 
rincipal Act, after sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be inserted, 
amely : — 

“(2/f ) Whoever contravenes or makes default in complying with any 
provision of this Act or of any condition subject to which exemption 
was granted under section 17 shall, if no other penalty is elsewhere

provided by or under this Act for such contravention or non- 
compliance, be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to 
three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, 
or with both.” 

6. Substitution of new section for section 17 in Act XIX of 1952— For 

section 17 of the principal Act, the following section shall be substituted, namc- 

iy : — 

«17 Power to exempt . — (/) The appropriate Government may, by noti- 
fication in the Official Gazette and subject to such conditions as 
may be specified in the notification, exempt from the operation of 
all or any of the provisions of any scheme — 

(a) any factory to which this Act applies if, in the opinion of the 

appropriate Government, the rules of its provident fund with res 
pect to the rates of contribution are not less favourable than those 
specified in section 6 and the employees are also in enjoyment of 
other provident fund benefits which on the whole are not less 
favourable to the employees than the benefits provided under this 
Act or any Scheme in relation to the employees in any other 
factory of a similar character; or 

(b) any factory if the employees of such factory are in enjoyment of 

benefits in the nature of provident fund, pension or gratuity and 
the appropriate Government is of opinion that such benefits, 
separately or jointly, arc on the whole not less favourable to such 
employees than the benefits provided under this Act or an\ 
Scheme in relation to employees in any other factory of a similar 
character. 

Explanation. — The following conditions shall be deemed to be alwav 
included in the conditions which may be specified in a notification 
under clause (a), namely : — 

(/) the amount of accumulations in the provident fund shall be invested 
in such manner as the Central Government may direct; 

(ii) the amount of accumulations to the credit of an employee in the 
provident fund shall, where he leaves his employment and 
obtains re-employment in another factory to which this Act 
applies, be transferred, within such time as may be specified 
in this behalf by the Central Government, to the credit of his 
account in the provident fund of the factory in which he is re- 
employed or, as the case may be, in the Fund established under 
the Scheme applicable to the factory. 

(2) Any Scheme may make provision for exemption of any person or class 
of persons employed in any factory to which the Scheme applies 
from the operation of all or any of the provisions of this Scheme, 
if such person or class of persons is entitled to benefits in the nature 
of provident fund, gratuity or old age pension and such benefits, 
separately or jointly, arc on the whole not less favourable than the 
benefits provided under this Act or the Scheme : 

Provided that no such exemption shall be granted in respect of a class ol 
persons unless the appropriate Government is of opinion that in* 
majority of persons constituting such class desire to continue to w 
entitled to such benefits.

ACT No. XXXIX OF 1953. 

THE DHOTIES (ADDITIONAL EXCISE DUTY) ACT, 1953. 

[16th December, 1953. ] 

n Act to provide for the levy and collection of an additional excise duty on 
dhoties issued out of mills in excess of the quota fixed for the purpose. 

Be it enacted by Parliament as follows: — 

1. Short title, extent and commencement. — (7) This Act may be called the 
ihoties (Additional Excise Duty) Act, 1953. 

(2) It extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and 
ashmir. 

(.?) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 26th day of October, 

953. 

2. Definitions. — In this Act, — 

(a) “dhoti” means any type of grey or bleached cloth of plain weave 

which — 

(/) is manufactured by a mill either wholly from cotton or partly from 
any other material; 

(//') contains coloured yam on its borders; 

(Hi) has a width ranging between twenty-eight inches and fifty-four inches; 

and 1 

(/v) is commonly known by that name; 

( b ) “mill” means any building or place in which cotton yam is spun and 

dhoties are manufactured by machinery moved otherwise than by 
manual labour, and includes every part of such building or place; 

(r) “permissible quota” means the quota referred to in section 3; 
ut) “quarter” means the period of three months ending on the last day of 
March, June, September and December. 

Permissible quota. — (7) The permissible quota of dhoties which may be 
issued out of any mill during any quarter, whether the dhoties were manufactur 
cd during that quarter or at any time previous thereto, shall be one-fourth of 
sixty per cent, of the total quantity of dhoties packed by that mill during the 
relevant period. 

Explanation I . — For the purposes of sub-section (7), the Central Govern- 
ment shall, by notification in* the Official Gazette, fix for all mills any period of 
twelve months which has expired before the commencement of this Act as the 
relevant period, and where any such period has been so fixed, the total quantity 
of dhoties packed by any mill during that period shall be determined with 
ference to the returns furnished in that behalf by the mill to the Textile Com- 
lissioncr to the Government of India under the Cotton Textiles (Control) 
•rdcr. 194X: 

Provided that where in the case of any mill, the relevant period so fixed is 
»t applicable by reason of the fact that the mill came into existence or com- 
aenccd working only during or after the expiry of the relevant period, the 
entral Government may, by a like notification, fix the permissible quota in 
espect thereof to be such quantity as, in its opinion, is reasonable, having 
®gard to the machinery and other equipment installed therein and to the other 
arcumstanccs of the case.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 

The institution of brothels has existed in many countries along with out 
from time immemorial but it has degenerated to its unthinkably cruel and hideou 
proportions mainly during the present century. Advanced countries all ovc 
the world and certain States in our own country also have taken measure), t 
stop and check this social evil; but the law in some of the States has bee) 
defective to the point of being ineffective. In some States no legislative actioj 
at all has been taken in this sphere so far. It, therefore, seems that the tint 
has come when legislation on all-India basis should be undertaken urgently i 
check this evil and to stop the immoral traffic in women and children rcsM ,,a « 
on the unchecked existence of brothels. ' The Bill seeks to make pro 1 
accordingly. 

SEETA PARMA NAN 

New Delhi ; 

The 8th April 1953.

an employer, under this Chapter but not paid by him shall be 
recoverable as delayed wages under the provisions of the Payment ol 
Wages Act, 1936 (IV of 1936).

as may be prescribed and requiring the registers to be made available

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 

The Government of India have ratified the I.L.O. Conventions Nos^ 89 a 
90 prohibiting employment of women and young Persons during night in fac on 
It is therefore, necessary to amend sections 66, 70 and 71 of the Factories A 
1948, to give effect to the provisions of the Conventions. 

2 The provisions in the Act relating to annual leave with wages have bf 
famine considerable difficulty particularly in determining the 12 months C< 
tinuous Service” for eligibility to leave with wages. It has, therefore, been 
necessarylo simplify the provisions so as to remove any cause for difference 
opinion between employers and workers. 

A This opportunity is also taken to incorporate in the Act certain otl 
amendments which would remove some practical diffculties experienced in 

, ■ c .u . Art durine the last four and a half years. The reasons 
amendments are, wherever necessary, given in the Notes on Clauses attached 

this Bill. V. V. Gil

Notes on clauses. 

Clause 2— The existing sub-clause k(iv) as it is worded, excludes some 
r»rpts,es including Government presses from the scope of the Act as 1 

the presses me uamg uove Qn . way of trade or for purposes 

onin 10 As it is not the intention to exclude them from the Act, it is neccss 
gam * tVir%»h-clause to make the intention clear. It is also necessary 
‘ameS thc dcfinton of “manufacture*. process” to cover separate pr« 
engaged in “composing types for printing .

Clause 3. -The existing section 4 empowers the State Governments to declare 
ilkrent departments of a tactory as separate factories. But there is no provision 
j enable two or more factories of the same occupier being declared as a single 
,ctory if an application for that purpose is made by the occupier. This clause 
rovides lot that* 

Clause 6. — The amendment is intended to make it clear that women and 
uung persons will be prohibited from cleaning, lubricating or adjusting any 
rime mover or transmission machinery while it is in motion only if such work 
fould expose them to risk of injury. 

Clause 7.— This clause makes it clear that all new machines should comply 
rith the requirements of encasement specified in sub-section (/) of section 20 and 

authorises State Governments to make rules specifying any further safeguards 
, be provided in respect of any class or description of machines. 

Clause 8. — Section 29 is being revised with a view to prescribing clearly the 
ifety requirements not only in respect ol cranes and other lifting machinery but 
Iso in respect of chains, ropes and lifting tackles. 

Clause 11. This clause will permit six hours’ work at a stretch without 
ny interval when the total number of hours to be worked on any day in a shift 
oes not exceed six. This is intended mainly to enable workers to avail them- 
:lves of half holidays in full on Saturdays wherever such holidays are allowed 
i will also permit newspaper printing presses to work their entire night shift of six 
ours at a stretch. 

Clause 12. The existing sub-section (2 ) empowers Stale Governments to 
:ame rules exempting any factory or class ot factories from ijie provisions relating 
) overlapping shifts. It has been tound not possible to prescribe by rules the 
m ol factories or the conditions under which the exemption can be granted 
) these factories as the grant of exemption has to be considered on the 
ircumstances of each case. A re-draft of the section has, therefore, become 
ecessary. 

Clause 13. The calculation of “cash equivalent of the advantage acciuing 
trough the concessional sale to workers of foodgrains and other articies’’ foi the 
urpose of computing the ordinary rate of wages of individual workers lor pay- 
tent of wages for overtime is creating difficulties. Calculation to be made in 
ach individual case depends on the size of the family, the actual rations bought 
s distinct from the maximum quantities the worker is entitled to buy and the 
dual difference. This involves considerable volume of clerical and eom- 
utational work and the only practical way of avoiding this is to lay down in the 
:ction itself that the cash equivalent will be computed on the basis of the 
ijxitnuni ration admissible tp a standard family of a specific number consump- 
an units. This clause is intended for this purpose. 

Clause 15 . — This amendment will liberalise the working of overtime. The 
“ended section will also enable continuous employment of workers in case 
>me ot the subsequent shift workers do not turn up in time. 

Clauses 17, 18 and 19 . — The amendments of sections 66, 70 and 71 arc 
,r ,llc purpose of bringing the provisions in conformity with the I.L.O. Con- 
ations Nos. 89 and 90 prohibiting employment of women and children during 
gnt in factories. 

Clause 20 . — Chapter VIII relating to leave with wages is revised in order 

simplify the existing provisions. According to the existing law, a worker 
MO put in 12 months’ “Continuous Service” for eligibility to leave with wages. 

|>e determination of “continuous service” has, however’ been causing consi- 
; fable difficulty as interruptions on account of various causes such as sickness, 


110 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, NOVEMBER 6, 1963 [Part Vt 


involuntary unemployment, etc., have to be reckoned with. A period of two 
hundred and forty days has now been fixed as the minimum attendance necessary 
during a calendar year to qualify for leave with wages. This condition of 
qualifying service will not be applicable to workers who are discharged or dis- 
missed by the employer in the course of the year. Proportionate leave will be 
grunted to workers whose service commences after the beginning of the calendar 
year. The annual leave with wages admissible under the Act will be exclusive 
ol holidays occurring during or at either end of the period of leave. The limit 
of the leave that can be carried forward has been raised. No prior notice will 
be necessary when a worker requires leave to cover a period of illness. The 
sums payable by an employer on account of leave with wages will be recoverable 
as if they were wages under the Payment of Wages Act. 

Clause 21 . — Section 93 has been recast to specify more clearly and definitely 
the responsibility for compliance with the various provisions of the Act between 
the owners of the premises and the occupier of the factory.

■STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 

The working of the Employees’ Provident Funds Act has brought oi 
certain defects. 

The principal defect relates to the application of the Act and the Schem 
There are considerable doubts regarding the expressions used in Schedule 
No authority has been prescribed for removing doubts and difficulty 
There is no power for applying the Scheme to a factory not covered by th 
Act even when the employer and the employees ask for such application. 

At present the employees of exempted factories are not entitled to tit 
benefits of nomination, protection against attachment or prior claim on th 
assets of an insolvent employer. It, is not possible to grant exemption t 
any factory from the operation of the Scheme on economic grounds. 

i 

There are also certain administrative difficulties to be set right. Thcr 
is no provision for inspection of exempted factories; nor is there any j>rovi 
sion for the recovery of dues from such factories. An employer enu dela; 
payment of provident fund dues without any additional financial liability 
No punishment has been laid down for contraventions of some of the prori 
aious of the Act. 

This Bill seeks primarily to remedy these defects.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 

The large scale immoral traffic in women and children that is going on 
our country has been a cause of grave anxiety for some time. Some States li 
Bombay, Madras, West Bengal and U.P. have taken measures for the suppn 
sion of immoral traffic, but it cannot be said that they are effective enough 
eradicate the evil, while a greater number of States have taken no legislati 
action so far. There is, therefore, an urgent need to adopt uniform legislati 
for the entire country to check the further growth of this evil.

STATEMENT OF OBJECTS AND REASONS. 

The object of the present Bill is to amend the First Schedule to the 
Indian Tariff Act, 1934 (XXXII of 1934), in order to grant protection to 
the Power and Distribution Transformers industry and to continue or dis- 
continue protection to certain other industries on the advice of the Tariff 
Commission.

Third and Final Forecast of Sugarcane Crop of 
West Bengal for 1952-53. 

[Note . — The figures of area and yield of sugarcane 
for this year except those of Darjeeling district 
and also the estimates of area only for last 
year except those of Darjeeling and Malda 
districts, as shown in this forecast are based 
on the results of sample survey conducted by 
# the State Statistical Bureau. The figures of 
yield for last year and that of Darjeeling 
district for this year as well as the area of 
Darjeeling district for both this year and last 
year and also of Malda district for last year are 
based on the reports received from the staff of 
ibis Directorate of Agriculture, West Bengal.] 


Seaton. — The weather conditions have generally 
* been favourable for the cultivation and growth of 
the crop in all the districts except Midnapore. J u 
the district of Cooch Behar the weather u Us 
unfavourable for a short period after the sowing 
time due to flood. 

Area and Yield. — The total area planted with 
sugarcane is estimated at. 52,300 acres this year 
compared to 46,300 acres last year. The total out. 
turn of sugarcane for the State as a whole 
estimated at 10,38,300 tons this year compared to 
8,19,800 tons last year. Calculated on the basis ot 
the gur/cane ratio 1:10, the fixed standard of the 
State as a whole, the gross outturn in terras of o U r 
is estimated ijt 1,03,830 tons this year as against 
81,980 tons last year. The average outturn j>er 
acre of cane for the State as a whole is estimated 
at 540*40 mds. this year compared to 481 *97 nub. 
last year.

for Director of Agriculture, West Bengal.

directorate of agriculture, 
WEST BENGAL 

Calcutta, the 26th June 1953. 

ird and Final Foreoast of Spring Oilseed Crops 
of West Bengal for 1952-53. 

The figures of linseed for this year and 

of rape and mustard for both this year and 
last year except those of Darjeeling district 
shown in this forecast are based on the results 
of sample survey and crop cutting experi- 
ments conducted by the State Statistical 
Bureau. The figures of linseed for last year 
and of “other oilseeds” for both this year and 
last year and also of “rape and mustard” for 
both this year and last year in the district of 
Darjeeling are based on the reports received 
from the staff of this Directorate of Agri- 
culture, West Bengal.] 

\rea and yield. — The total area under the spring 
iced crops (except sesamum for which separate 
ecasts are published) is estimated at 3,10,700 
ob this year compared to 2,83,800 acres last 
tr. The average outturn per acre of different 
■in£ oilseeds for the State as a whole is estimated 
4 96 maunds this year compared to 4*75 maunds 
t year. 

Linseed. — 63,900 acres have been estimated to be 
rier linseed this year compared to 44,900 acres 
t year. The total outturn of linseed for the 


State as a whole is estimated at 9,600 tons this 
year compared to 7,600 tons last year. The 
average outturn per acre of the crop for the State 
as a whole is estimated at 409 maunds this year 
compared to 4 64 maunds last year. 

The figures of the two consecutive years are not 
comparable, last year’s estimates being not based 
on sample survey as mentioned in the note above. 

Rape and mustard. — 2,26,200 acres have been 
estimated to be under rape and mustard this year 
compared to 2,17,800 acres last year. The total 
outturn of the crop for the State as a whole is 
estimated at 43,900 tons this year compared to 
38,900 tons last year. The average outturn per 
acre of the crop for the State as a whole is esti- 
mated at 5*28 maunds this year compared to 4 86 
maunds last year. 

Other oilseeds (exoept til).— 20,600 acres have 
been estimated to be under ‘‘other oilseeds” this 
year compared to 21,100 acres last year. The total 
outturn of the crop for the State as a whole is 
estimated at 3,100 tons this year compurcd to 
3,000 tons last year. The average outturn per 
acre of the crop for the State as a whole is estimated 
at 413 maunds this year compared to 3 82 maunds 
last year. 

D. BASU,
