CORPORATION OF CALCUTTA 

Calcutta, the 5th September .1958. 

NOTICE. 

In supersession of the Rules published in the Calcutta Gazette , dated the 10th 
July 1952, the Corporation of Calcutta propose (as per their resolution, dated the 
4th September 1952), under section 20 of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951, as 
amended by the Calcutta Municipal (Amendment) Act, 1952, to make the rules 
horeinbolow appearing for determining the powers, duties and functions of the 
Standing Committees of the Corporation. 

The draft rules are published in compliance with section 533 of the Calcutta 
Municipal Act, 1951, and will be taken into consideration on or ajfter the 24th 
September 1953, and any objection or suggestion with respect thereto which may 
be reeoivcd by the undersigned before that date, shall be considered. A copy of 
the draft rules will be kept in the office room of the Secretary to the Corporation 
for public inspection. 

B. K. SEN, Commissioner. 


Rules under stction 26(1) of tho Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951, proscribing the 
powers, duties and functions of the Standing Committees, constituted under 
the said Act. 


(In supersession of the Rules published in tho Calcutta Gazette , dated the 10th July 

1952.) 


1. (a) The powers, duties and functions of the Standing Committee dealing 
with Education hereinafter referred to as the Standing Education Committee shall 
be as set out in Schedule T hereto annexed. 

(b) The decision of tho Standing Education Committee shall be final in respect 
of matters against which the word “final” appears in the said Schedule. All other 
proceedings of the Standing Education Committee shall be subject to confirmation 
by the Corporation. 

2. (a) The powers, duties and functions of the Standing Committee dealing 
with Accounts hereinafter referred to as tho Standing Accounts Committee shall 
be as set out in Schedule TI hereto annexed. 

(6) The decision of the Standing Accounts Committee shall be final in respect 
of matters against which the word “final” appears in the said Schedule. All other 
proceedings of the Standing Accounts Committee shall be subject, to confirmation 
by the Corporation. 

3. (a) The powers, duties and functions of the Standing Committee dealing 
with Taxation and Finance hereinafter referred to as the Standing Finance ( Committee 
shall bo as set out in Schedule III hereto annexed. 

(5) The decision of the Standing Finance Committee shall be final in respect, 
of matters against which tho word “final” appears in the said Schedule. All other 
proceedings of the Standing Finance' Committee shall be subject to confirmation 
by the Corporation. 

4. (a) The powers, duties and functions of the Standing Committee dealing 
with Health hereinafter referred to as the Standing Health Committee shall be as 
set out in Schedule IV annexed hereto. 

(i b ) The decision of the Standing Health Committee shall be final in respect 
of matters against which the word “final” appears in the said Schedule. All other 
proceedings of tho Standing Health Committee shall be subject to confirmation 
by the Corporation. 

5. (a) The powers, duties and functions of tho Standing Committee dealing 
with the Town Planning and Improvement hereinafter referred to as the Standing 
Town Planning and Improvement Committee shall be as set out in Schedule V 
annexed hereto. 


(6) The decision of the Standing Town Planning and Improvement Committee 
■hall be final in respect of matters against which the word final appears m h 
aaid Schedule. All other proceedings of the Standing Town Planning and Improve- 
ment Committee Bhall be subject to confirmation by the Corporation.

6. (a) The powers, duties and functions of the Standing Committeo dealing 
with Works hereinafter referred to as the Standing Works Committee shall be as 
sot out in Schedule VI annexed hereto. 

(b) The decision of the Standing Works Committee Rhall bo final in respect 
of matters against which the word “final” appears in the said Schedule. All other 
proceedings of the Standing Works Committee shall be subject to confirmation 
by the Corporation. 

7. (a) The powers, duties and functions of the Standing Committee dealing 
with Buildings hereinafter referred to as the Standing Buildings Committee shall 
be as set out in Schedule VII annexed hereto. 

(b) The decision of the Standing Buildings Committeo shall bo final in respect 
of matters against which the word “final” appears in the said Schedule. All other 
proceedings of the Standing Buildings Committee shall bo subject to confirmation 
by the Corporation. 

8. (a) The powers, duties and functions of the Standing Committee dealing 
with Public Utilities and Markets hereinafter referred to as the Standing Public 
Utilities and Markets Committee shall bo as set out in Schedule VIII annexed hereto. 

(b) The decision of the Standing Public Utilities and Markets Committee shall 
bo final in respect of matters against which the word “final” appears in the said 
Schedule. All other proceedings of the Standing Public Utilities and Markets 
Committee shall be subject to confirmation by the Corporation. 

9. (a) The powers, duties and functions of the Standing Committee dealing 
with Water Supply hereinafter referred to as the Standing Water Supply Committee 
shall be as set out in Schedule IX hereto. 

(b) The decision of the Standing Water Supply Committee shall l>e final in 
respect of matters against which the word “final” appears in the said Schedule. All 
other proceedings of the Standing Water Supply Committee shall be subject to 
confirmation by the Corporation. 

10. (a) The powers, duties and functions of the Standing Borough Committees 
shall be as set out in Schedule X annexed hereto. 

(b) The decision of the Standing Borough Committees shall be final in respect 
of matters against which the word “final” appears in the said Schedule. All other 
proceedings of the Standing Borough Committees shall be subject to confirmation 
by the Corporation.

CALCUTTA IMPROVEMENT TRUST 

Calcutta, 1st September 1958. 

The publication under section 180 of the Calcutta 
Improvement Act of the abstract of the annual 
accounts of the Trust suspended since 22nd Feb- 
ruary 1945, by notification No. 496M., under the 
Defence of India Rules, is now resumed. The 
account last published was tor the year 1942-48. 
The accounts for the years 1948-44, 1944-45 and 
1945-46 which were dul^ audited by auditor ap- 
pointed by the Government are now published to 
comply with the provisions of section 186 ol the 
Act. 


S. K. GUPTA, 
Chairman.

the figures oi acreage and yield rate of this year 
shown in this forecast have been based on the

rates for last year are based on the reports as 
received from the staff of the Agriculture 
Directorate. ]

the whole favourable for the cultivation 
growth of the crop in almost all the district))

estimated to be under “Tur” (Arhar) this 
compared to 41,100 acres last year. The total

estimated at 16,870 tons this year compare 
12,800 tons last year. The average outturn 
acre of the crop for the State as a whole has, 
estimated at 6 ’62 maunds this year compare 
8 *47 maunds last year.

Calcutta, the 10th October 1953. 

NOTICE. 

In supersession of the Rules published in the Calcutta Gazette* dated 
the 10th July 19>>2, the Corporation at their meeting' held on the 5th 
October 1953, adopted under section 2b read with section 533 of the 
Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951, as amended by the Calcutta Municipal 
(Amendment) Act, 1953, the following Rules ior determining the powers, 
duties aud functions of the Standing Committees constituted uncier the 
Calcutta Municipal Act, 19ol, and the said Rules are published herein below 
under section 535 of the said Act. 

B. GHOSH, Secy. 

Rules under seotion 26(1) of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951, prescribing

DIRECTORATE OF AGRICULTURE,, WEST 
BENGAL. 

Calcutta, the 25th June 1953. 

Sfoond Forecast of Winter Potato and the 
Preliminary Forecast of 8ummer Potato Crops 
of West Bengal for the year 1952-53. 

[Note . — The figure** of last year and this year 
in respect of Winter Potato except those of 
Darjeeling district as shown in the forecast are 
based on the results of Sample Survey conducted 
by the State Statistical Bureau. The estimates of 
Darjeeling district for both this year and last 
year shown in the forecast have been estimated 
bv the Directorate of Agriculture, West Bengal. 
The figures of Summer Potato shown in this 
forecast are also based on the reports received from 
the staff of this Directorate.] 

ScMOn. — The weather conditions were not 
favourable at the sowing time in the districts of 
Burdwan, Jalpaiguri and Darjeeling, while in 
other districts the weather was favourable. The 
subsequent weather conditions were however 
favourable for the growth of the crop in the dis- 
tricts of 24-Parganas, Murshidabad, Burdwan, 
Midnapore and West Dinajpur. 


Area and yield.— Winter Potato.— 96,200 aen 
have been estimated to be under Winter p 0 taj 
this year compared to 99,800 and 100,500 acn 
reported respectively in the corresponding and j 
final forecasts of last year. The decrease in are 
is reported to have been due to unfavourab] 
weather condition at the sowing time and l 0 i 
price of jute which caused some reduction in th 
income of cultivators for harvesting in notn* 
cultivation. P 1 

The total outturn of the crop for the State as 
whole is estimated at 412,500 tons this year a 
against 433,400 and 434,900 tons reporte 
respectively in the corresponding and in fim, 
forecast of last year. 

The average outturn per acre of the crop lor th 
State as a whole is estimated at 116*73 maund 
this year as against 118*22 and 117:78 maund 
reported respectively in the corresponding and i] 
final forecast of last year. 

Summer Potato. — Summer Potato grows only jj 
the hilly regions of Darjeeling district. The tota 
area under Summer Potato in these regions ig 
estimated at 4,100 acres this year compared to 
2,800 and 3,500 acres reported respectively in th* 
corresponding and in the final forecast of last year

IECTORATE OF AGRICULTURE! WEST 

* BENGAL. 

Calcutta, the 6th October 1953. 

nvninary Forecast of Autumn Rice Crop of 
West Bengal for 1953-54. 

f/ k>. The figures of area this year are the first 

estimates of State Statistical Bureau, these 
being based on the analysis of half sample “A” 
of their random Sample Survey, while those 
of last year have been taken from the hint 
year’s final forecast based on the analysis ol 
complete materials of the Sample Survey con- 
ducted by the Bureau. The yield rates of 
last year have been taken from the last year’s 
final forecast based on crop cutting experi- 
ments carried out by the State Statistical 
Bureau, while those of this year are based on 
the eye-estimates of the staff of the Agricul- 
ture Directorate, it being too early for crop 
cutting experiments] . 


Season.— The weather has generally been favour- 
able for the sowing and growth of the crop in the 
district except Darjeeling. It has however been 
reported from some districts that certain areas have 
been damaged by insect-posts, rice-bug and heavy 
rainfall and flood though the weather conditions 
have on the whole been favourable. 

Area and yield. — 1 ,6^9,600 acres have been 
estimated to be under Autumn rice this year as 
against 1,395,300 acres and 1,350,800 acres report- 
ed respectively in the corresponding ami final fore- 
cast of last year. The average yield of cleaned 
rice per acre tor the State as a whole is tentatively 
estimated to be 9-19 mds. this year compared to 
8*97 maunds, the final estimate of last year. The 
increase) in area ami expected yield of Autumn rice 
is mainly due to fall in area of jute ami favourable 
weather conditions. 

I). HASH, 

for Director of Agriculture, 
West Bengal.
